judged_text: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` executes the entire feed poll synchronously inside the retrieve_topic sidekiq job, but PollFeed's execute guard re-checks `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` — already true — and `poll_feed` then does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network fetch plus a PostCreator DB write per item, all inside a job whose sole purpose is to fetch one URL. Each first-time embed request triggers a full-feed import inside the retrieve_topic worker; a large feed makes the worker block for minutes and hammers the third-party feed server on every new embedded URL, and if the feed fetch raises (e.g. timeout) the RetrieveTopic job fails with retry instead of falling through to fetch_http.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (no Sidekiq enqueue) before `fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` per item (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This means a first-time embed retrieval can trigger a full feed fetch/import unrelated to the single `@embed_url`, creating a significant performance/load/scalability concern and coupling embed retrieval latency to feed size/availability. The finding’s point about exceptions from `open(...)` aborting the flow is also plausible since there’s no rescue around the PollFeed call in `perform_retrieve`, but the diff doesn’t specify intended fallback behavior, making this more of an architecture/robustness concern than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.
